#!/bin/bash

# Usage: ./count_lines.sh <keyword> [directory]
# Counts total lines in all .txt files (recursively) that contain the keyword.

KEYWORD="${1:-keyword}"
DIR="${2:-experiment}"

if [ -z "$KEYWORD" ]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <keyword> [directory]"
    exit 1
fi

# Find all .txt files recursively, count lines containing the keyword
TOTAL=$(grep -r -l --include="*.txt" "$KEYWORD" "$DIR" 2>/dev/null | xargs -r grep -c -- "$KEYWORD" 2>/dev/null | awk '{sum += $1} END {print sum}')

echo "Total lines containing keyword '$KEYWORD' in $DIR: $TOTAL"
EOF

#!/bin/bash

# Usage: ./count_lines.sh <keyword> [directory]
# Counts total lines in all .txt files (recursively) that contain the keyword.

KEYWORD="${1:-keyword}"
DIR="${2:-experiment}"

if [ -z "$KEYWORD" ]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <keyword> [directory]"
    exit 1
fi

# Recursively search all .txt files, count lines containing the keyword.
# grep -h prints matches without filename; wc -l counts matching lines.

echo "Total lines containing keyword '$KEYWORD' in $DIR: $TOTAL"
EOF
